newsitem.title: GERMANY: FOCUS-Russia takes step toward cutting debt burden.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Russia takes step toward cutting debt burden.

text.p: Russia took a small, but meaningful step in reducing its massive debt burden on Thursday, making the final downpayment of a debt rescheduling plan ahead of schedule, Deutsche Bank AG said.

Deutsche, which chairs the advisory committee of the London Club of bank creditors for Russia, said Russia's Vnesheconombank last Monday transferred $50 million to a trust account held with the Bank of England.
The payment brings total transfers from the bank on behalf of Russia to two billion dollars since Russian debt was rescheduled in 1995.
Sources familiar with the talks said Russia had originially intended to make the payment at the end of the first quarter of 1997.
They said the early payment was a further small signal that Russia was trying to gain the confidence of capital markets and present istelf as a good debtor.
Russia in November 1995 reached a deal with its commercial bank creditors to reschedule about $25 billion in debt principal and about nine billion dollars in interest.
